Special ordered sets and complementarity

Source: R/special-constraints.R
opt_sos1.Rd

opt_sos1(): at most one element of x is nonzero. opt_sos2(): at most two elements are nonzero and they are adjacent in the order given by weights. opt_complementarity(): \(x_i y_i = 0\) elementwise for nonnegative variables, the complementarity condition \(0 \le x \perp y \ge 0\), as SOS1 pairs.

Usage

opt_sos1(model, x, weights = NULL, name = NULL)

opt_sos2(model, x, weights = NULL, name = NULL)

opt_complementarity(model, x, y, name = NULL)

Arguments

model

An opt_model().

x, y

Decision variables (a block or a slice of one).

weights

Distinct weights that order the set; defaults to seq_along(x).

name

Optional name.

Value

An opt_special_constraint reference (a list of them for opt_complementarity()), invisibly.

Details

SCIP handles these natively. For other mixed-integer solvers they are reformulated exactly with one binary per element (SOS1) or segment (SOS2), which requires finite bounds.

Examples

# piecewise linear interpolation of f(u) = u^2 on the grid 0, 1, 2, 3
m <- opt_model()
lam <- opt_variable(m, "lambda", dim = 4, lower = 0, upper = 1)
u <- opt_variable(m, "u")
opt_constraint(m, sum(lam) == 1)
opt_constraint(m, u == sum(0:3 * lam))
opt_constraint(m, u >= 1.5)
opt_sos2(m, lam)
opt_objective(m, sum((0:3)^2 * lam))
opt_objective_value(opt_solve(m))  # 2.5, the interpolant at 1.5
#> [1] 2.5
